title: Continuity of perfect sheaf dg Hom under finite coefficient enlargement
statement:
Fix universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $D$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $A$ be a commutative $D$-algebra which is not of finite type over $D$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], let $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}D$ be separated and of finite type [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-morphism-conventions], and let $W\subseteq Y$ be a quasi-compact open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. For every commutative $D$-algebra $B$, put $\mathcal C_B=\mathcal O_W\otimes_D R_B$, with the functorial coefficient resolutions, quasi-coherent sheaf dg categories and local perfectness of [def-sfb-dg-coefficient-realization]. Use left dg localizations and derived extension of [def-sfb-sheaf-dg-module-localization].

Let $E$ be a finite type commutative $D$-algebra equipped with a $D$-algebra map $E\to A$. Let $I_E$ be the set, ordered by inclusion, of finite type $D$-subalgebras $B\subseteq A$ containing the image of $E$ and strictly containing the image of $D$. This is a small nonempty directed partially ordered set in the chosen universe. For perfect $P,Q\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal C_E)$, write $P_B=\mathcal C_B\otimes_{\mathcal C_E}^{\mathbf L}P$ and $Q_B=\mathcal C_B\otimes_{\mathcal C_E}^{\mathbf L}Q$, and similarly define $P_A,Q_A$. With transition maps on Hom induced by derived extension and its canonical composition comparisons, the canonical map
$$\varinjlim_{B\in I_E}\operatorname{Hom}_{D_W(\mathcal C_B)}(P_B,Q_B)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{D_W(\mathcal C_A)}(P_A,Q_A)$$
is a bijection. The colimit of sets is the disjoint union of the stage Hom sets modulo equality at a common later stage. The comparison is induced by derived extension to $A$. No flatness or injectivity of $E\to A$ is assumed; only the displayed subalgebra transition maps are inclusions.

source.place: Agent sheaf-dg refinement of Tag 09RE (lemma-descend-homomorphisms), case (1); its affine calculation and Mayer--Vietoris argument motivate this statement. The tag itself treats ordinary derived scheme objects, not these non-flat derived coefficient algebras. Standard resolution continuity is cotangent.tex Tag 08PM (definition-standard-resolution) and Tag 08S9 (lemma-colimit-cotangent-complex), refined in lem-sfb-standard-normalized-resolution-filtered-colimit.

proof.text: Write $L_{C,B}=\mathcal C_C\otimes_{\mathcal C_B}^{\mathbf L}-$. By [lem-sfb-ringed-dg-scalar-adjunction] these functors exist, are exact, and commute with open restriction, for left modules by opposite algebras. Their canonical composition comparison comes from composing their adjunction bijections: restriction along a composite is the composite restriction, so both extensions are left adjoints to the same functor. This also pins the unit, counit, shift and composition comparisons. A regular module is graded-flat and homotopically flat, since tensoring with it is the identity. Thus [lem-sfb-sheaf-dg-hflat-computation] identifies its derived extension with the new regular module. Exactness and additivity preserve finite sums, shifts and cones, and functors preserve the retract equation $ri=1$. Consequently extension preserves local perfection. By [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] these affine coordinate rings are finite type over $D$. On affine opens its values have quasi-coherent underlying cohomology by [lem-sfb-affine-dg-coefficient-module-comparison].

source.place: Tag 09RE (lemma-descend-homomorphisms), affine calculation and finite-open Mayer--Vietoris induction; agent adaptation to sheaf dg coefficients.

proof.text: The image of $E$ has a finite set of $D$-algebra generators. Since $A$ is not finite type over $D$, choose $a\in A$ outside the image of $D$. Adjoining $a$ and those generators gives an index of $I_E$. Uniting two finite generating sets gives a common upper bound, and adjoining any specified element shows that the union of the stages is $A$. These subalgebras form a set in the stipulated universe. For any $B_0\in I_E$ the tail $B\supseteq B_0$ is cofinal: replace a stage by its subalgebra together with $B_0$. The disjoint-union/eventual-equality presentation therefore gives the same colimit on the tail. By Step 1 we can replace $P,Q$ by $P_{B_0},Q_{B_0}$ on that tail. None of $B\in I_E$ or $A$ is the exceptional algebra $D$ in [def-sfb-dg-coefficient-realization]. On an affine open $Z=\operatorname{Spec}S$, [lem-sfb-standard-normalized-resolution-filtered-colimit] consequently gives $C_A=\varinjlim_B C_B$, for $C_B=S\otimes_D R_B$, together with homogeneous lifts and eventual detection of every finite family of differential and algebra equations.

source.place: Tag 09RE (lemma-descend-homomorphisms), affine calculation and finite-open Mayer--Vietoris induction; agent adaptation to sheaf dg coefficients.

proof.text: First suppose $Z=\operatorname{Spec}S$ is an affine open of $W$. The structure map is locally of finite type, so [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] makes $S$ finite type over $D$. Fix $B_0\in I_E$ and work on its cofinal tail. By [lem-sfb-affine-dg-coefficient-module-comparison], $P_{B_0}|_Z,Q_{B_0}|_Z$ correspond to retracts of finite-cell $C_{B_0}$-modules $F,G$. Here a finite-cell module has a finite filtration with quotients finite sums of shifts of the regular module. Each graded quotient is finite free and its graded splitting is obtained by lifting its finitely many basis vectors. Choosing these splittings identifies the underlying graded modules of $F,G$ with finite direct sums of shifted regular modules. This choice need not commute with differentials. The affine equivalence identifies all subsequent derived scalar extensions with the module extensions. We prove continuity for these finite-cell modules in all degrees, then pass to the given retracts.

source.place: Tag 09RE (lemma-descend-homomorphisms), affine calculation and finite-open Mayer--Vietoris induction; agent adaptation to sheaf dg coefficients.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-dg-semifree-bimodule-tensor-computation] to compute derived extensions of $F,G$ by ordinary dg tensors, naturally for module maps. Use opposite algebras to pass from its right-module convention to left modules; a left action becomes the graded-opposite right action $x\cdot c^{\mathrm{op}}=(-1)^{|x||c|}cx$. Finite-cell modules have property (P), extending the finite filtration by constant terms. By [lem-sfb-dg-property-p-homotopically-projective] and [lem-sfb-dg-homotopically-projective-hom-derived], their derived Hom groups are $H^0$ of the signed graded Hom complexes; applying the same assertion to every shift computes all degrees. Relative to the graded bases of Step 3, the degree-$q$ Hom group from $F_B$ to $G_B$ is a finite direct sum of homogeneous components of $C_B$. Its differential is $\delta h=d_Gh-(-1)^qhd_F$, a finite matrix formula in the coefficient differential and the fixed differential matrices of $F,G$. Derived extension sends a representative matrix to its coefficientwise image, since the ordinary tensor computations are natural. This describes the actual comparison maps, not merely an abstract group isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 09RE (lemma-descend-homomorphisms), affine calculation and finite-open Mayer--Vietoris induction; agent adaptation to sheaf dg coefficients.

proof.text: For the matrix complexes in Step 4, a degree-$q$ cocycle over $C_A$ has finitely many entries. Lift them to one stage using [lem-sfb-standard-normalized-resolution-filtered-colimit]. The finitely many entries of $\delta h=0$ vanish at a common later stage, so this stage matrix is already a cocycle. This proves surjectivity on $H^q$. If a stage cocycle becomes a boundary, write its image as $\delta k$ over $C_A$, lift the finitely many entries of $k$ to one later stage, and enlarge once more to make the finitely many equations $h=\delta k$ hold. Thus its cohomology class is zero at that later stage. Subtracting two cocycles proves eventual equality and hence injectivity. This proves continuity for the finite-cell pair in every integer degree. It uses no flatness of the coefficient transition maps: the finite matrices are computed after derived extension, and coefficient continuity detects the equations themselves.

source.place: Tag 09RE (lemma-descend-homomorphisms), affine calculation and finite-open Mayer--Vietoris induction; agent adaptation to sheaf dg coefficients.

proof.text: For the retracts, choose $P_{B_0}|_Z\xrightarrow{i_P}F\xrightarrow{r_P}P_{B_0}|_Z$ and $Q_{B_0}|_Z\xrightarrow{i_Q}G\xrightarrow{r_Q}Q_{B_0}|_Z$ with $r_Pi_P=r_Qi_Q=1$. The map $f\mapsto i_Q f r_P$ identifies Hom of the retracts with the fixed subgroup of the idempotent $e(h)=i_Qr_Q h i_Pr_P$ on $\operatorname{Hom}(F,G)$, with inverse $h\mapsto r_Qh i_P$. Apply this also with shifted targets. Extension preserves these equations and the matrix continuity is natural for composition. Any fixed element at the limit has a stage representative $h$ by Step 5; since $e(h)=h$ at the limit this equality holds at a later stage by its injectivity assertion. Conversely two fixed representatives with the same image agree later by that assertion. Therefore continuity holds for the retracts. Through the affine equivalence of Step 3 this proves the required comparison on every affine open, simultaneously for all shifts and all perfect pairs. No splitting of a derived idempotent into a strict dg idempotent was used.

source.place: Tag 09RE (lemma-descend-homomorphisms), affine calculation and finite-open Mayer--Vietoris induction; agent adaptation to sheaf dg coefficients.

proof.text: Use [lem-pqf-finite-affine-cover-qc-open] to choose a finite affine cover of $W$. Prove the comparison in every degree, for every perfect pair on every open of $Y$ covered by at most $r$ affine opens, by induction on $r$. The empty open has the zero category and the comparison is bijective. The case $r=1$ is Steps 3--6, for any finite coefficient starting algebra mapping to $A$. For the induction step write $Z=O\cup V$, where $O$ has an $(r-1)$-member affine cover and $V$ is affine. The structure map to $\operatorname{Spec}D$ is separated; thus [lem-weil-pbc-separated-affine-open-intersection] shows $T=O\cap V$ is covered by at most $r-1$ affine opens. Restrictions of perfect objects and their shifts are perfect by the local definition. The induction hypothesis applies on $O,T$ and the affine case applies on $V$, in every degree.

source.place: Tag 09RE (lemma-descend-homomorphisms), affine calculation and finite-open Mayer--Vietoris induction; agent adaptation to sheaf dg coefficients.

proof.text: For each stage and at $A$, apply [lem-sfb-sheaf-dg-open-hom-mayer-vietoris] to the cover $Z=O\cup V$ and $P,Q$. Its derived-scalar naturality, including the boundary, makes these rows a directed diagram mapping to the row over $A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-abelian-groups-exact], their filtered colimit row is exact. Around degree $n$, denote its five terms by $L_1\to L_2\to M\to R_1\to R_2$: these are the two degree-$(n-1)$ local groups, the overlap group in that degree, the global degree-$n$ group, the two local degree-$n$ groups, and the overlap degree-$n$ group, respectively. The row over $A$ has the corresponding terms with primes. The four vertical maps on $L_1,L_2,R_1,R_2$ are isomorphisms by Step 7. The middle vertical map $m:M\to M'$ is exactly the canonical comparison of the item, with the shift $n$.

source.place: Tag 09RE (lemma-descend-homomorphisms), affine calculation and finite-open Mayer--Vietoris induction; agent adaptation to sheaf dg coefficients.

proof.text: For completeness the five-term diagram gives bijectivity as follows. Given $x'\in M'$, lift its image in $R'_1$ uniquely to $r\in R_1$. Its image in $R_2$ is zero, since its image in $R'_2$ is zero and $R_2\to R'_2$ is injective. Exactness gives $x\in M$ mapping to $r$. Then $x'-m(x)$ comes from $L'_2$, and lifting that element along $L_2\to L'_2$ corrects $x$ to a preimage of $x'$. If $m(x)=0$, injectivity on $R_1$ makes $x$ come from some $l\in L_2$. Its image in $L'_2$ maps to zero in $M'$, hence comes from $L'_1$. Lift this element to $L_1$; subtract its image from $l$. The difference has zero image in $L'_2$, hence is zero by injectivity on $L_2$. Thus $x=0$. This completes the induction, and on $Z=W,n=0$ proves the claimed Hom bijection.

source.place: Tag 09RE (lemma-descend-homomorphisms), affine calculation and finite-open Mayer--Vietoris induction; agent adaptation to sheaf dg coefficients.

proof.text: The group colimit used in Step 8 has the stated underlying set presentation: represent elements at stages, add at a common upper bound, and identify representatives exactly when their images agree at a common later stage. These rules define an abelian group and have the group-colimit universal property, since compatible homomorphisms send representatives to their given images. They also have the set-colimit universal property after forgetting the operations. Consequently the comparison just proved is the specified set comparison. All its maps are induced by the derived extensions of Step 1, so composition and passage to $A$ are the ones in the statement.
